signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-22 reality-web Epic 51 comparison i18n)
evidence: reality-web is an explicitly 4-locale public portal (sk, cs, de, en — messages/{en,sk,cs,de}.json; every other user-facing component uses next-intl's useTranslations), but two entire Epic 51 comparison components import NO translation function and render hardcoded English user-facing strings.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/CompareButton.tsx — no `useTranslations` import at all. Hardcoded visible text: :47 title={inComparison ? 'Remove from comparison' : 'Add to comparison'} (tooltip), :62 {inComparison ? 'Comparing' : 'Compare'} (button label), :66 'Maximum 4 properties. Remove one first.' (role=alert warning). Non-Slovak/Czech/German users on the localized portal see raw English on the primary compare CTA that appears on every listing card.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonTray.tsx — no `useTranslations` import at all. Hardcoded visible text: :23 '{n}/4 properties to compare', :25 'Clear all', :36 alt={`Thumbnail for ${listing.title}`}, :46 aria-label={`Remove ${listing.title} from comparison`}, :68 `Compare {n<2 ? '(need at least 2)' : '${n} properties'}`. The tray is a fixed, always-visible floating element once any listing is added.

Fix: wire both components through useTranslations('comparison') (the namespace already exists — ComparisonView.tsx:28 uses it and the sibling ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx uses t('loading')/t('loadError')), add the missing keys to messages/*.json, and pluralize the count strings via next-intl. Landable in the cloud runner (pure TS/tsx + JSON message files, no backend, no build required to author).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonView.tsx:117 — showToast() does `setTimeout(() => setToast(null), 3000)` with no handle stored and no clearTimeout. Because each call starts an independent uncancelled timer, two toasts fired within 3s stack their timers: the FIRST timer fires ~partway through the SECOND toast's lifetime and clears it early (e.g. copy-link then share-url in quick succession dismisses the newer toast prematurely). The timer also is never cleared on unmount, so a toast that is dismissed by navigating away leaves a pending setState on an unmounted component.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/CompareButton.tsx:34 — same pattern: `setTimeout(() => setShowMaxWarning(false), 3000)` with no cleanup; if the button unmounts (listing scrolls out of a virtualized list) within the 3s window the callback still runs.

Fix: store the timer id in a useRef, clearTimeout the previous one before starting a new one, and clear it in a useEffect cleanup on unmount. Standard toast/transient-warning hygiene. Landable in the cloud runner (pure tsx).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:47 — for each user-supplied shared id the loader does `return response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>` with NO runtime shape validation, then pushes the result straight into the comparison store (addToComparison). The ids come entirely from a shared/bookmarked URL (sharedIds), so the response shape is effectively attacker/stale-data-controlled.

Downstream, ComparisonView.tsx renders these objects and dereferences required numeric/object fields directly — e.g. :107 getValue: (l) => (l.area > 0 ? Math.round(l.price / l.area) : undefined) and the price/pricePerSqm rows assume l.price/l.area/currency exist. A 200 response with a partial or wrong-typed body (missing price, features/photos wrong-typed) is truthy and passes the `if (result.value)` check at :59, so a malformed listing can render NaN/blank cells or throw during render.

This is the same class of soft-corruption the sibling SSR listing detail page explicitly defends against: app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx routes every body through parseListingDetail() precisely because 'a 200 does not guarantee a well-formed body'. The shared-comparison client path has no equivalent guard — inconsistent hardening across two consumers of the same endpoint.

Fix: validate each fetched listing against a lightweight shape check / zod-style parser (or reuse a ListingSummary normalizer) before addToComparison, dropping malformed entries the same way bad ids are already dropped at :63. Landable in the cloud runner (pure tsx).
